data.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is a filament eruption centered near N25E65 which begins to lift off around 2026-05-29T23:30Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery. A subsequent opening of field lines is observed over the northeast limb around this time in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 imagery.

data.note: This CME is visible as a northwest partial halo in STEREO A COR2 imagery, and a northeast halo in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. Although no evidence of an eruption was visible on the Earth-facing disk, the Solar Orbiter STIX instrument, which was located at longitude -155 at the time of this event, observed the equivalent of a ~C9 flare peaking at 2026-05-30T08:01Z. Additionally, STEREO Ahead observed an increase in the 13-100 MeV protons starting around 2026-05-30T09:00Z, with a peak value of 0.02 pfu/MeV observed at 2026-05-30T10:15Z. It is possible the source is related to former Active Region 14436, located at N18E150 at the time of this event, based on prior activity from this region when it was on the Earth-facing disk. Additionally, the triangulated CME measurement places the CME in the vicinity of former Active Region 14436.

The source is likely a prominence over the SW limb observed first in STEREO A EUVI 304 as early as 2026-05-30T15:15Z, and in SDO AIA 171 as field line movement starting around 2026-05-30T17:00Z.

The source of this outflow/CME appears to be a filament eruption with moving/opening field lines starting around 2026-05-31T05:00Z in SDO/AIA 171/304 to the NE with full liftoff closer to 2026-05-31T07:00Z.

data.note: This CME visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source of this CME is a filament eruption best seen in STEREO A EUVI 304 to the SW with associated brightening and in STEREO A EUVI 195 starting around 2026-05-31T11:15Z. Additional moving/opening field lines and views of the filament are seen in SDO/AIA and GOES SUVI wavelengths beyond the SW limb starting around 11:46Z. Based on STEREO A EUV imagery, it is possible the source area of this filament eruption was near former AR 14443 (~S17W110 to W118) at the time of the eruption.

data.note: CME first seen to the SW by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-05-31T16:53Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME appears much wider in STEREO A COR2 than it does in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source of this event is a filament eruption seen from along the SW limb (approx. S30W145) in STEREO A EUVI 304 with lift-off beginning at approx. 2026-05-31T15:00Z. Field line opening is also visible in GOES SUVI 284 and SDO AIA 193.

The source of this event is a small eruption of filament ejecta seen originating from Active Region 14447 (S17W64) beginning at approx. 2026-05-31T16:00Z as seen in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304. This CME was likely heavily deflected to the South.

The source of this event is a small eruption of filament material from Active Region 14447 (S17W65) beginning at approx. 2026-05-31T19:08Z as seen in GOES SUVI 304.

This CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap which began at 2026-05-31T19:38Z. The source of this event is a filament eruption seen centered at approx. S40E50 beginning at approx. 2026-05-31T19:22Z with lift off at approx. 2026-05-31T20:12Z as seen in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304. This filament was likely deflected to the North by a large coronal hole to the South of this eruption.

The source of this event is wide opening field lines seen originating from beyond the NE limb beginning at approx. 2026-05-31T22:57Z in SDO AIA 171, 193 and GOES SUVI 284.

data.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely related to an eruption from AR 4455 (centered near N25E35) as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and near the northeast limb in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery starting around 2026-06-01T03:00Z. An opening of field lines is seen over the northeast limb in SDO AIA 171/193, GOES SUVI 171/195/284, and STEREO A EUVI 195 imagery. Additionally, dimming is seen northeast of the eruption site in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 193 imagery and post eruptive arcades begin to form around 2026-06-01T05:00Z.

data.note: CME first seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-06-01T19:00Z. This CME is also seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. This is the slower and wider of two overlapping CMEs. There are a series of coronal signatures likely associated with these two CMEs. This first is some ejecta seen over the W limb in SDO AIA 304 beginning around 2026-06-01T17:57Z. There are also some post-eruptive arcades best seen in STEREO A EUVI starting around 2026-06-01T18:55Z to the W of a small, SW coronal hole. Another coronal signature is a field line movement seen over the SW in STEREO A EUVI 195, GOES SUVI 284, and SDO AIA 171/193 beginning around 2026-06-01T18:30Z.

data.note: CME first seen to the North by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-06-02T03:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. This event is blocked by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. The source of this CME is a C1.8 flare from Active Region 14455 (N15E09) seen peaking at 2026-06-02T02:50Z in SDO AIA 131. A small jet of filament ejecta is visible in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304 in association with this flare, and is heavily deflected to the North, likely due to this region sitting just North of a coronal hole.
